record.original_question: Study binary operations that preserve random strings or random sequences.

evidence.quote: 20. Study binary operations which preserve random strings/sequences. (T. Odor)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A binary string is a finite element of $\{0,1\}^*$ and a binary sequence is an element of $\{0,1\}^\omega$. Fix a universal prefix-free Turing machine and let $K(\cdot)$ denote prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity. A finite string $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ is called (Levin–Chaitin) random if $K(x) \ge n - O(1)$, and an infinite sequence $X \in \{0,1\}^\omega$ is called Martin-Löf random if there is a constant $c$ such that $K(X\!\upharpoonright\!n) \ge n - c$ for every $n$.

A binary operation on strings is a computable map $\ast : \{0,1\}^* \times \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}^*$, and a binary operation on sequences is a (Turing-computable) map $\star : \{0,1\}^\omega \times \{0,1\}^\omega \to \{0,1\}^\omega$.

Characterize all binary operations $\ast$ on strings and $\star$ on sequences with the following randomness-preservation property: there is a constant $c$ (resp. the conclusion holds for almost-every pair) such that whenever both arguments are random (in the appropriate sense above), the output is also random. In particular, describe the structural form of such operations and determine whether interesting nontrivial examples exist beyond projections, computable measure-preserving transformations, and the join operation appearing in van Lambalgen's theorem.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem attributed to T. Ódor in the algorithmic information theory open-problems literature. While related partial results are known (van Lambalgen's theorem for the join operation, and preservation of Martin-Löf/Schnorr/Kurtz randomness under almost-everywhere computable measure-preserving transformations), no general characterization of randomness-preserving binary operations appears in the literature. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmically random sequence - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Van Lambalgen's Theorem states that α ⊕ β is Martin-Löf random iff α is ML-random and β is ML-random relative to α.
status_evidence.claim: Known partial result on a specific binary operation (join) preserving randomness.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic randomness - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: Martin-Löf, Schnorr and Kurtz randomness are preserved under almost everywhere computable measure-preserving transformations.
status_evidence.claim: Known preservation results exist for measure-preserving transformations, but no general characterization of randomness-preserving binary operations is established.
